verses.text: The LORD's ark stayed in Philistine territory for seven months.
The Philistines called their priests and diviners and asked, “What should we do with the LORD's ark? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs.”

They answered, “If you send back the ark of Israel's God, don't send it back empty. Be sure to send a guilt offering with it. Then you'll be healed, and you'll know why his hand hasn't lifted from you.”

They asked, “What guilt offering should we send him?” The priests and diviners answered, “Five gold tumors and five gold mice, one for each Philistine ruler, because the same plague struck you and your rulers.
Make models of the tumors and of the mice ravaging your land, and give glory to Israel's God. Maybe he'll lift his hand from you, your gods, and your land.
Why harden your hearts the way Pharaoh and the Egyptians did? Once God did wonders among them, didn't they let the people leave?
Now get a new cart ready and take two nursing cows that have never worn a yoke. Hitch them to the cart and shut their calves up at home, away from them.
Put the LORD's ark on the cart. Put the gold objects you're sending as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send the cart on its way.
Watch where it goes. If it heads toward its own territory at Beth Shemesh, Israel's God brought this disaster on us. If it doesn't, we'll know his hand didn't strike us and it happened by chance.”
The men did as they were told. They hitched two nursing cows to the cart and shut their calves up at home.
They put the LORD's ark on the cart with the box holding the gold mice and the gold models of their tumors.
The cows went straight along the road to Beth Shemesh, lowing as they went. They didn't turn right or left. The Philistine rulers followed them as far as the border of Beth Shemesh.
The people of Beth Shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the ark, they were overjoyed.
The cart rolled into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh and stopped beside a large stone. The people split up the cart for wood and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
The Levites took down the LORD's ark and the box with the gold objects and set them on the large stone. That day the people of Beth Shemesh brought burnt offerings and other sacrifices to the LORD.
The five Philistine rulers saw what happened and went back to Ekron that same day.
The gold tumors the Philistines sent as a guilt offering to the LORD were one each for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

The gold mice represented all the Philistine towns ruled by the five leaders, whether fortified towns or country villages, as far as the large stone where they set the LORD's ark. That stone is still in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh today.
The LORD struck down fifty thousand and seventy men of Beth Shemesh because they had looked inside the LORD's ark. The people mourned because the LORD had struck them with such a great slaughter.
The people of Beth Shemesh asked, “Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? Where can the ark go from here?”
They sent messengers to Kiriath Jearim to say, “The Philistines have returned the LORD's ark. Come down and take it up to your town.”
